stem: How did electric light change the working day for Americans?

stimulus.source_note: Harper's Weekly, June 24, 1882, "The Electric Light in Houses — Laying the Tubes for Wires in the Streets of New York," drawn by W. P. Snyder. Public domain. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Laying_electric_lines_under_street_Edison_Pearl_Street_Utility_June_21_1882_Harpers_Weekly.png
stimulus.text: The image is a page from Harper's Weekly, June 24, 1882, titled "THE ELECTRIC LIGHT IN HOUSES — LAYING THE TUBES FOR WIRES IN THE STREETS OF NEW YORK." The top panel, "Laying the Electrical Tubes," shows workers digging a New York street and lowering thick tubes into the ground. The bottom panel, "Testing Tubes for Insulation," shows a worker at a tripod instrument and others handling coiled wire. An inset at the top right shows a worker pouring insulation.

options.text: It ended factory work, since machines could run without people
options.misconception: Background: machines still needed workers; electric light let people work longer hours, it did not replace them.

options.text: It made the working day shorter, since light cost more than candles
options.misconception: Background: electric light let work run past sundown, so the working day grew longer, not shorter.

options.text: It changed nothing, since most Americans already worked at night
options.misconception: Background: before electric light, most work ended at sundown; night work was rare and costly.

options.text: It stretched the working day past sundown, into hours that had been dark

rationales.A: Background: factories still needed workers to run the machines. Electric light let those workers keep working after dark, it did not send them home.
rationales.B: Background: electric light was brighter and steadier than candles, and it let work run on after sundown. The working day stretched longer, not shorter.
rationales.C: Background: before electric light, the working day ended at sundown for most people. Night work was rare because lamps were dim and costly.
rationales.D: Background from the books: Edison's advances allowed for the extension of the workday, which previously ended at sundown, and the wider availability of electricity. Light after dark meant work after dark.
rationales.general:
Ask what the sun used to decide: quitting time.
1. Background: before electric light, most work stopped at sundown because lamps were dim and costly.
2. Background: Edison's light let the workday run past sundown, and factories and shops stayed open into the night.
3. Background: the day itself got longer, not just brighter.
Remember: a light that beats the sun changes the clock, not just the room.
